title: Smooth presentation criterion for general algebraic stack morphisms
statement: Let $S$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme] in the universes of [def-weil-size-convention], and let $f:\mathcal X\to\mathcal Y$ be a morphism of algebraic stacks over $S$ [def-sfb-algebraic-moduli-stack]. Morphisms, $2$-commutative diagrams and $2$-fibre products use [def-sfb-stable-pointed-moduli-groupoids]. Algebraic spaces use [def-trf-algebraic-space]. A map of algebraic spaces is smooth when it is smooth on compatible etale scheme charts, using [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms]. A representable map of fibred groupoids is smooth when every scheme base change is a smooth algebraic-space projection. Surjective means that every object over a field lifts, up to isomorphism, after a field extension. Consider diagrams $U\xrightarrow{q}V$ over $f$, with $U,V$ algebraic spaces and representable smooth vertical maps $a:U\to\mathcal X$ and $b:V\to\mathcal Y$. The following conditions are equivalent: (A) every such diagram for which the induced map $U\to\mathcal X\times_{\mathcal Y}V$ is representable smooth has smooth $q$; (B) some such diagram with $a$ surjective has smooth $q$. Requiring $U,V$ to be schemes in both conditions gives equivalent conditions. These are the smooth-chart definition of smoothness for $f$. If $\mathcal X,\mathcal Y$ are algebraic spaces, these conditions are equivalent to ordinary smoothness of their map. If $f$ is representable by algebraic spaces, these conditions are equivalent to smoothness of $\mathcal X\times_{\mathcal Y}T\to T$ for every scheme $T\to\mathcal Y$. No Deligne--Mumford, quasi-compactness, separation, Noetherian or finite-type hypothesis is imposed.

source.place: Tag 06FM (lemma-local-source-target), specialized to smooth; Tag 075U (definition-smooth) and its introductory verification of the hypotheses. Scheme-chart form by etale atlas refinement. The etale-stack convention is criteria.tex Tag 076V (lemma-stacks-etale).

proof.text: First relate the two meanings of smoothness for a map $r:A\to B$ of algebraic spaces. Ordinary smoothness implies representable smoothness: every scheme base change is an algebraic space and is ordinarily smooth by the space base-change lemma. Conversely suppose $r$ is representable smooth. Choose a surjective etale scheme atlas $V\to B$ and a surjective etale scheme atlas $U\to A\times_BV$. The scheme-test hypothesis makes $A\times_BV\to V$ smooth. The etale presentation criterion, applied with target chart $\mathrm{id}_V$, makes $U\to V$ smooth. The etale covering calculus makes $U\to A$ surjective etale. Apply the same presentation criterion to $U\to V$ over $r$ to obtain ordinary smoothness of $r$. Its hypothesis that scheme smoothness is etale local on source-and-target is exactly the scheme locality lemma. This also identifies scheme smoothness with its algebraic-space extension. Thus below the representable calculus can be applied to ordinary smooth space maps, and its space-valued outputs can be read as ordinarily smooth. Finally relate the two meanings of surjectivity for a representable map $a:U\to\mathcal X$ from an algebraic space. If every scheme base change of $a$ is surjective on field-valued point classes, then for an object $x$ over a field $K$ the base change $U\times_{\mathcal X}\operatorname{Spec}K$ is a nonempty space over $\operatorname{Spec}K$; any field-valued point of it, over an extension $L\supseteq K$, is a lift of $x|_L$ to $U$ up to isomorphism. Conversely, if objects over fields lift after extension, then for a scheme $T\to\mathcal X$ and a point $t\in T$ the restriction to $\kappa(t)$ lifts over some $L\supseteq\kappa(t)$, which is an $L$-valued point of $U\times_{\mathcal X}T$ above $t$. Thus the surjectivity of the statement, of the representable calculus and of the atlases of an algebraic stack agree.

source.place: Tag 06FM, representable-space comparison specialized to smooth; spaces-morphisms.tex Tag 03MJ (lemma-local-source-target), and spaces-descent.tex Tag 0429 with spaces-morphisms.tex Tag 03ZE

proof.text: Write $A_{\rm sch},B_{\rm sch}$ for the two tests restricted to schemes. Assume $A_{\rm sch}$ (the same construction applies assuming A). Choose a representable smooth surjective scheme atlas $V\to\mathcal Y$. The stack $\mathcal W=\mathcal X\times_{\mathcal Y}V$ is algebraic by algebraicity of stack fibre products; a scheme is here a discrete algebraic stack with its identity atlas. Choose a representable smooth surjective scheme atlas $U\to\mathcal W$. Representable base change and composition show that $U\to\mathcal X$ is smooth and surjective, since $\mathcal W\to\mathcal X$ is the base change of $V\to\mathcal Y$. The induced map $U\to\mathcal X\times_{\mathcal Y}V$ is precisely the chosen atlas, so this diagram is among those tested by $A_{\rm sch}$. Its map $q:U\to V$ is smooth. This proves $B_{\rm sch}$ with both $U,V$ schemes.

Assume B, witnessed by $q:U\to V$, $a,b$, with $a$ smooth surjective and $q$ smooth. Let $q':U'\to V'$, $a',b'$ be any diagram tested by A, and write $c':U'\to\mathcal X\times_{\mathcal Y}V'$ for its smooth induced map. Form the algebraic spaces $E=V\times_{\mathcal Y}V'$, $D=U\times_{\mathcal Y}V'$ and $P=U\times_{\mathcal X}U'$. They are spaces by representable pullback over a space, using respectively $b',b',a$. There is a cartesian square with top $P\to U'$, bottom $D\to\mathcal X\times_{\mathcal Y}V'$, and right side $c'$. Indeed an object of its pullback is an object $u$ of $U$, an object $u'$ of $U'$, and an isomorphism $a(u)\simeq a'(u')$; its $V'$-component and compatibility are supplied by $q'(u')$ and the image of that isomorphism in $\mathcal Y$. Forgetting the redundant $V'$-component is inverse to inserting $q'(u')$. Thus $P\to D$ is representable smooth. Also $D\to E$ is the base change of $q$ by $E\to V$, so it is ordinarily smooth. The projection $E\to V'$ is the base change of $b$, hence representable smooth. By step 1 all three maps are ordinarily smooth.

source.place: Tag 06FM (lemma-local-source-target), proof of (2) => (1), the comparison diagram and its cartesian square

proof.text: The composite $P\to D\to E\to V'$ is smooth by composition in the representable calculus and step 1. It equals $q'\circ p$ for $p:P\to U'$. The map $p$ is the base change of the smooth surjective map $a$, hence smooth surjective. For each point $u'$ of $U'$, choose a point $z$ of $P$ above it. The smooth-source point-locality lemma, applied to $q'$ and $p$ at $z$, gives that $q'$ is smooth at $u'$. These smooth neighbourhoods cover $U'$, so $q'$ is smooth: on any compatible etale scheme charts this is source locality of scheme smoothness, as supplied by the scheme locality lemma. Consequently B implies A. Only $a$ is required to be surjective; neither $b$ nor $b'$ has been assumed surjective.

source.place: Tag 06FM (lemma-local-source-target), final descent in (2) => (1); spaces-descent.tex Tag 06F2 (lemma-smooth-smooth-local-source)

proof.text: A implies $A_{\rm sch}$ by restricting its universal quantifier, $A_{\rm sch}$ implies $B_{\rm sch}$ by step 2, $B_{\rm sch}$ implies B by allowing algebraic spaces, and B implies A by steps 3--4. These four implications prove all four conditions equivalent. Calling this condition smoothness is precisely the smooth-chart definition: it is independent of both the presentation and whether schemes or spaces are used.

source.place: Tag 075U (definition-smooth), using the equivalence of Tag 06FM

proof.text: If $\mathcal X=X$ and $\mathcal Y=Y$ are algebraic spaces and $f$ is ordinarily smooth, it is representable smooth by step 1. In any diagram of A the map $U\to X\times_YV$ and the projection $X\times_YV\to V$ are then representable smooth, so their composite $q$ is ordinarily smooth by the calculus and step 1. Conversely, if A holds, take $U=X$, $V=Y$, and both vertical maps identities. Identities are representable smooth (their scheme tests are identity maps, smooth directly from the scheme definition). The induced $X\to X\times_YY$ is an isomorphism, hence smooth for the same reason. The conclusion of A is exactly ordinary smoothness of $f$. This proves the algebraic-space comparison, without using a scheme atlas as if it were an identity.

source.place: Tag 06FM (lemma-local-source-target), paragraph comparing with maps of algebraic spaces

proof.text: Suppose now that $f$ is representable and B holds. For an arbitrary scheme $T\to\mathcal Y$ put $W=\mathcal X\times_{\mathcal Y}T$, $U_T=U\times_{\mathcal Y}T$, $V_T=V\times_{\mathcal Y}T$. These are spaces: $W$ by representability of $f$, $U_T$ by that of $f\circ a$, and $V_T$ by that of $b$. The map $U_T\to W$ is smooth surjective, being a base change of $a$, and $V_T\to T$ is smooth, being a base change of $b$. Further $U_T\to V_T$ is the base change of $q$. Explicitly, $U\times_V(V\times_{\mathcal Y}T)\simeq U\times_{\mathcal Y}T$: a triple $(u,v,t)$ with $q(u)=v$ and $b(v)\simeq t$ is sent to $(u,t)$ with the composed isomorphism, and its inverse inserts $v=q(u)$. Therefore $U_T\to V_T\to T$ is smooth by the representable calculus and step 1. Smooth-source point locality along the smooth surjection $U_T\to W$ shows that $W\to T$ is smooth, just as in step 4. No cover of T, no quasi-compactness of any map, and no surjectivity of $V_T\to T$ is used.

source.place: Tag 06FM (lemma-local-source-target), final paragraph, specialized to smooth using smooth-source locality

proof.text: Conversely, if $f$ is representable and every scheme base change $\mathcal X\times_{\mathcal Y}T\to T$ is smooth, then $f$ is representable smooth by the definition in the statement. Given any diagram of A, its projection $\mathcal X\times_{\mathcal Y}V\to V$ is a representable smooth base change of $f$. Composing it with the stipulated representable smooth map from $U$ gives representable smooth $q:U\to V$. Step 1 makes $q$ ordinarily smooth. Thus A holds, completing the representable comparison. All constructions and arguments used arbitrary algebraic stacks and arbitrary scheme tests throughout.
